newsitem.title: USA: Wheatland, Calif., sees default on bond payments.
newsitem.headline: Wheatland, Calif., sees default on bond payments.

text.p: The city of Wheatland in northern California expects on Friday to default on its bond payments for the first time, the city administrator said.

"It is certainly my belief that default will occur. There is not enough in our reserves to make the payments," said Wheatland Administrator Clay Castleberry. "The city is disappointed that it has to happen, but it is not within our control to change it."
Wheatland's $2.1 million of Mello-Roos bonds were issued in 1990 to pay for sewer and highway improvements in areas planned for development of hundreds of housing units.

The Wheatland development has, however, been marred by financial problems due to delinquencies by major property owners. Last November, Wheatland was forced to draw down on bond reserves to pay investors.
"We're continuing foreclosure actions against those properties that didn't make their payments," Castleberry said on Thursday.
In August, the city sent notices to bondholders warning of the likelihood of a default on the Mello-Roos bond payments on November 1.

Castleberry said bond reserves have been depleted and that the city did not have the funds to cover the shortfall and fully pay bondholders on Friday. Castleberry believed the default would be the first ever by the small city.

The Wheatland bond issue had been the subject of a Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry. But in late May, the SEC told the city it was dropping its probe. The SEC is still investigating the deal's underwriter, San Francisco-based First California Capital Markets Group Inc.
